result: Loss of BMP signaling (Put RNAi) results in ectopic Notch pathway activity even when the Notch ligand Delta (Dl) is depleted. The authors show that Put and Dl double RNAi suppresses ISC-like tumor formation but still activates Notch signaling in progenitor cells, suggesting Notch activation is independent of Delta ligand when BMP signaling is lost.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 raises a technical limitation, noting that 'depending on how fast both proteins are depleted, it may be that only one of them (put, for example) is inactivated and affects the fate decision prior to the other one (Dl) being depleted. Therefore, it is difficult to definitively conclude that the decision is independent of Dl ligand.' This critique questions the interpretation of the double knockdown experiment, though the data itself is not disputed.

result: Neither Mad RNAi nor Numb RNAi alone leads to ISC loss, but combined Mad and Numb double RNAi results in significant decrease in ISC numbers and increase in enteroblasts, suggesting stem cell loss due to precocious differentiation.
evaluation: All reviewers accept this finding. Reviewer 1 states the results 'demonstrate an important role of Numb in maintaining ISC number during regeneration and a genetic interaction between Mad and Numb during homeostasis.' Reviewer 3 notes 'the results and statistical analyses provides believable evidence' for the genetic interaction. No concerns were raised about these RNAi experiments.

result: mad1-2 numb4 double mutant clones are significantly smaller than control clones, with ~40% lacking ISCs entirely and many containing only differentiated enterocytes. In contrast, mad1-2 or numb4 single mutant clones retain ISCs similar to controls.
evaluation: Reviewers accept the clonal analysis data showing genetic interaction. Reviewer 1 notes 'ISC loss was observed in 40% of mad, numb double mutant clones, whereas 60% of these clones had an ISC' and raises no concerns. Reviewer 3 acknowledges the data are 'highly coherent' though notes the phenotypes are 'weaker than many other mutants previously studied,' which is a contextual observation rather than a critique of validity.

result: Using the RGT two-color tracing system, the authors show that Mad and Numb double RNAi guts have much lower ISC/ISC symmetric division (11%) and much higher EB/EB symmetric differentiation division (37%) compared to controls, while single knockdowns show minimal changes.
evaluation: Reviewer 1 explicitly describes this result: 'They then employed a two-color tracing system called RGT to look at the outcome of ISC divisions... mad, numb double mutant clones had much lower ISC/ISC (11%) and much higher EB/EB (37%).' The reviewer concludes this demonstrates that 'loss of Numb in moderate BMP loss of function mutants increased symmetric differentiation which lead caused ISC loss.' No concerns were raised about this analysis.

result: numb mutant clones (both numb4 and numb15 alleles) show moderately increased frequencies of ISC-lacking clones compared to controls under homeostatic conditions, though most clones can grow to large sizes and retain ISCs.
evaluation: Reviewers accept this finding as demonstrating a mild homeostatic role for Numb. Reviewer 1 states the authors 'reported that numb15 and numb4 clones had a moderate but significant increase in ISC-lacking clones compared to control clones, supporting the model that Numb plays a role in ISC maintenance.' Reviewer 3 notes 'a weak reduction of ISC number' in numb mutants, which is consistent with the authors' interpretation that Numb is largely dispensable under homeostasis.

result: Bleomycin treatment, which causes fluctuation in BMP ligand production, results in dramatic increase in ISC-lacking clones (43-45%) and reduced clone size in numb mutants. DSS treatment, which does not affect BMP fluctuation, shows no such increase.
evaluation: All reviewers strongly support this regeneration finding. Reviewer 1 states 'After bleomycin treatment, there was a significant increase in ISC-lacking clones and a significant decrease in clone size in numb4 and numb15 clones compared to control clones' and concludes the results demonstrate 'an essential role of Numb in ISC maintenance during regeneration.' Reviewer 3 notes 'A much stronger phenotype was observed when numb mutants were subject to treatment of tissue damaging agents Bleomycin' and that this 'led to highly significant reduction of ISC in clones.'

result: Numb acts in parallel with BMP signaling as a backup mechanism: Numb is largely dispensable under normal homeostasis due to predominant BMP signaling, but becomes critical for ISC self-renewal when BMP signaling is compromised.
evaluation: This interpretive model is accepted by all reviewers. Reviewer 2 states the study 'provides an interesting model of a "back up" protection mechanism for ISC maintenance' and notes 'Experiments are consistent with these previous publications while also extending our understanding of how Numb functions in the ISC.' The editor summarizes that 'the authors demonstrate the ISC maintenance is reduced when both BMP signaling and Numb expression is reduced,' supporting the parallel pathway model.

result: The authors propose a model where asymmetric Numb segregation provides a fail-safe mechanism for ISC self-renewal by offsetting BMP pathway fluctuation. Under homeostasis, combined differential BMP and Numb activities drive asymmetric divisions, but when both are compromised, symmetric differentiation divisions lead to ISC loss.
evaluation: Reviewers accept this mechanistic model as a reasonable interpretation of the data. Reviewer 2 states the study 'provides an interesting model of a "back up" protection mechanism for ISC maintenance' with no objections to the proposed mechanism. Reviewer 3 notes 'the results overall support their claim' regarding the backup mechanism. The model is presented as speculative interpretation (Figure 7) and reviewers treat it as such without challenging its logic given the experimental evidence.

result: numb mutant clones do not contain Pros+ enteroendocrine cells, consistent with previous findings that numb is required for EE fate regulation.
evaluation: This finding is accepted without comment from reviewers, consistent with established literature. The authors cite previous work (Sallé et al., 2017) and reviewers do not question this observation.
